chapter_title_ka: ნახვა არაბთა მეფისაგან მის ყმისა ვეფხის-ტყაოსნისა
chapter_title_en: Seeing by the King of the Arabians of the Knight Clad in the Panther's Skin
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Resting by a stream after the hunt, Rostevan and Avtandil behold a weeping stranger knight clad in a panther's skin (Tariel). Lost in sorrow, the knight ignores Rostevan's envoys, effortlessly routs the royal guards when they attempt to seize him, and vanishes without a trace. Queen Tinatin counsels her grieving father with Christian-Neoplatonic theology ('Why should the Creator of good make evil?', Stanza 113) and advises sending searchers across the earth.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ნახეს უცხო მოყმე ვინმე, ჯდა მტირალი წყლისა პირსა,
შავი ცხენი სადავითა ჰყვა ლომსა და ვითა გმირსა;
ხშირად ესხა მარგალიტი ლაგამ-აბჯარ-უნაგირსა.
და ცრემლსა ვარდი დაეთრთვილა, გულსა მდუღრად ანატირსა.
stanzas.english_translation: They saw a certain stranger knight; he sat weeping on the bank of the stream, he held his black horse by the rein, he looked like a lion and a hero; his bridle, armour and saddle were thickly bedight with pearls; the rose (of his cheek) was frozen in tears that welled up from his woe-stricken heart.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: One of the most iconic stanzas in Georgian literature ('Nakhes utskho moqme vinme...'): the Arabian court catches sight of the mysterious stranger knight (Tariel) weeping on the riverbank, holding his black steed by the rein, his bridle, armor, and saddle encrusted with pearls, and the 'rose' of his face covered with the frost of hot tears.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მას ტანსა კაბა ემოსა, გარე-თმა ვეფხის ტყავისა,
ვეფხის ტყავისა ქუდივე იყო სარქმელი თავისა,
ხელთა ნაჭედი მათრახი ჰქონდა უსხოსი მკლავისა;
და ნახეს და ნახვა მოუნდა უცხოსა სანახავისა.
stanzas.english_translation: His form was clad in a long coat over which was thrown a panther's skin, his head, too, was covered with a cap of panther's skins; in his hand he held a whip thicker than a man's arm. They looked and liked to look at that wondrous sight.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: This stanza gives the poem its title ('Vepkhistkaosani'): the stranger wears a coat and cap of panther's skin with the fur turned outward ('gare-tma vepkhis tqavisa')—which, as Tariel later explains, he wears because the panther's spotted beauty reminds him of Nestan-Darejan—and holds a forged whip thicker than a man's arm.

stanzas.english_translation: A slave went forth to speak to the knight of the woestricken heart, who, weeping with downcast head, seems not a spectacle for jesting; from a channel of jet (his eyelashes) rains a crystal shower. When (the slave) approached, he could by no means bring himself to speak a word (to Tariel).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan dispatches a royal attendant to summon the stranger, who weeps 'a rain of crystal from channels of jet' (clear tears through jet-black eyelashes). Struck with awe by the knight's tragic majesty, the attendant is rendered speechless.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ვერა ჰკადრა საუბარი, მონა მეტად შეუზარდა,
დიდხან უჭვრეტს გაკვირვებით, თუცა გული უმაგარდა;
მოახსენა: “გიბრძანებსო”, ახლოს მიდგა, დაუწყნარდა.
და იგი ტირს და არა ესმის, მისგან გაუუმეცარდა.
stanzas.english_translation: The slave was much perturbed; he dared not address him. A long time he gazed in wonder till his heart was strengthened; then he said: "(The king) commands thee (to attend him)." He (the slave) came near, (and) greeted him gently; he (Tariel) wept on and heard not, he knew not that (the slave) was there.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Gathering his courage, the attendant conveys the king's summons, but Tariel is so deeply absorbed in his grief that he neither hears nor notices him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მის მონისა არა ესმა სიტყვა, არცა ნაუბარი,
მათ ლაშქართა ზახილისა იყო ერთობ უგრძნობარი,
უცხოდ რადმე ამოსკვნოდა გული ცეცხლთა ნადებარი;
და ცრემლსა სისხლი ერეოდა, გასდის, ვითა ნაგუბარი.
stanzas.english_translation: He heard not a word of the slave, nor what he said; he was wholly unconscious of the shouting of the soldiers, he was sobbing strangely, his heart burnt up with fires; tears were mingled with blood, and flowed forth as from floodgates.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Oblivious even to the clamor of the nearby army, Tariel sobs as tears mixed with blood pour from his eyes like a dammed pool ('nagubari').

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
სხვაგან ქრის მისი გონება, მისმან თავისა წონამან!
ესე მეფისა ბრძანება ერთხელ კვლა ჰკადრა მონამან.
არცა დააგდო ტირილი, არცა რა გაიგონა მან,
და არცა გახლიჩა ბაგეთათ თავი ვარდისა კონამან.
stanzas.english_translation: Elsewhither his mind was wafted, by the weight of his head! Once again the slave uttered the king's message, but (Tariel) ceased not from weeping and heard him not, nor was the rose-bouquet (of speech) plucked from his lips.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Tariel's mind is soaring elsewhere (with Nestan-Darejan); even when the attendant repeats the royal command, the 'rosebud of his lips' does not part to utter a word.

stanzas.english_translation: Since he answered not, the slave went back and said to Rosten: "I have told him what you said, but he will not listen. Mine eyes were dazzled as by the sun; my heart was sorely troubled. I could not make him hear a word though I have tarried there so long."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: The attendant returns to Rostevan, reporting that his eyes were dazzled as if by the sun and that the stranger was completely deaf to his words.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფე გაკვირდა, გაცაწყრა, გული უც მისთვის მწყრომარე;
გაგზავნა მონა თორმეტი, მისი წინაშე მდგომარე,
უბრძანა: “ხელთა აიღეთ აბჯარი თქვენ საომარე,
და მიდით და აქა მომგვარეთ, ვინ არის იქი მჯდომარე”.
stanzas.english_translation: The king wondered, he was wroth, he was vexed in heart against him. He sent the twelve slaves standing before him; he commanded: "Take weapons of war in your hands; go and bring hither him who sits yonder."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Offended by what appears to be a breach of royal deference in his own domain, King Rostevan orders his twelve elite armed guards to bring the stranger before him by force.

stanzas.english_translation: The slaves went forth, they drew nigh to him, their armour clanked. Then indeed the knight started up, he wept still more woefully; he raised his eyes and looked round, he saw the band of warriors. But once he said, "Woe is me!" and spoke no word more.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Only the clanking of the approaching guards' armor rouses Tariel from his reverie; seeing the host of warriors, he utters a single 'Woe is me!' ('Va meo!').

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
თვალთა ხელი უკუივლო, ცხელნი ცრემლნი მოიწურნა,
ხრმალ-კაპარჭი მოიმაგრა, მკლავნი გაიმამაცურნა;
ცხენსა შეჯდა, - მონათამცა საუბარნი რად იყურნა! -
და სხვასა მხარსა გაემართა, მათი ჭირი არ განკურნა.
stanzas.english_translation: He passed his hands over his eyes, he wiped away the hot tears, he made fast his sabre and quiver, and braced his strong arms. He mounted his horse--why should he heed the words of slaves? He wended his way elsewhither, and healed not their troubles.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Tariel wipes away his tears, fastens his sword and quiver, mounts his black horse, and rides off in another direction without deigning to argue with the guards.

stanzas.english_translation: The slaves stretched forth their hands to seize that knight; he fell upon them--alas! even their enemies would have pitied them; he beat one against another, he slew them without raising (on high) his hand, some with his whip he smote, cleaving them down to the breast.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: When the guards reach out to seize him, Tariel—without even drawing his sword—strikes them against one another and cleaves others to the chest with a single blow of his forged whip, illustrating the Prologue's ideal of the lover as 'overcomer of mighty adversaries' (Stanza 23).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფე გაწყრა, გაგულისდა, ლაშქარნიცა შეუზახნა,
მან მდევართა მიწევნამდის არ უჭვრიტნა, არცა ნახნა;
რაზომნიცა მიეწივნეს, ყოვლნი მკვდართა დაასახნა,
და კაცი კაცსა შემოსტყორცნა, როსტან ამად ივაგლახნა.
stanzas.english_translation: Wrathful was the king, and annoyed; he shouted to the slaves. The youth looked not back nor heeded his pursuers till they were upon him; as many as overtook him he made to look like dead men, he threw down man on man; Rosten lamented thereat.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: When Rostevan orders the wider army in pursuit, Tariel ignores them until they overtake him, then hurls horseman upon horseman.

stanzas.english_translation: The king and Avt’handil mounted to follow the youth. Proud and haughty, his form swayed to and fro, his steed was like Merani, the sun shone brightly on the field; he perceived that the king pursued him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan and Avtandil mount their horses to pursue him personally. Tariel rides his steed (compared to 'Merani', the mythical winged steed of Georgian folklore) until he perceives that the King himself is riding after him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ცნა, მეფე მოვიდაო, ჰკრა მათრახი მისსა ცხენსა.
მასვე წამსა დაიკარგა, - არ უნახავს თვალსა ჩვენსა; -
ჰგვანდა ქვესკნელს ჩაძრომილსა, ანუ ზეცად ანაფრენსა.
და ეძებდეს და ვერ ჰპოებდეს კვალსა მისგან წანარბენსა.
stanzas.english_translation: When he saw that the king was come, he struck his horse with his whip; in that very moment he was lost, our eyes see him not; he seemed to have sunk into an abyss or flown to heaven; they sought, but could find no trace of his course.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Out of chivalric respect for royal dignity (as Tariel later explains to Avtandil in Stanza 294, he refused to raise his hand against a monarch), Tariel strikes his horse with his whip and vanishes in the blink of an eye.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
კვალი ძებნეს და უკვირდათ ვერ პოვნა ნაკვალევისა,
აგრე კვალ-წმიდად წარხდომა კაცისა, ვითა დევისა;
ლაშქარნი მკვდართა სტიროდეს, სწრაფა აქვთ წყლულთა ხვევისა.
და მეფემან ბრძანა: “ვნახეო მიზეზი ლხინთა ლევისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: His footprints they sought, and marvelled to find no trace. Thus, leaving no vestige, the man passed away like a Devi. The soldiers mourned for their dead; they hastened to bind up the wounded. The king said: "I have seen cause for loss of joy."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Unable to find a single hoofprint, the soldiers marvel that the stranger vanished like a supernatural 'Devi' (demon/giant of Georgian mythology), while Rostevan laments that his joy has been shattered.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ბრძანა: “ღმერთსა მოეწყინა აქანამდის ჩემი შვება,
ამად მიყო სიამისა სიმწარითა დანავღლება,
სიკვდილამდის დამაწყლულა, ვერვის ძალ-უც განკურნება;
და მასვე მადლი, ესე იყო წადილი და მისი ნება”.
stanzas.english_translation: He said: "God is weary of the happiness I have had hitherto, therefore He turns my pleasure into the gall of bitterness; He has wounded me unto death, none can cure me. Such, by His grace, is His will and desire."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: In his grief, Rostevan attributes his sudden misfortune to God growing weary of his long happiness, setting up the theological debate with Tinatin in Stanza 113.

stanzas.english_translation: Thus he spoke, and returned; he went frowning away. They summoned not to the lists; groan was mingled with groan. Each ceased from the chase wherever he was following it. Some said: "He is right!" others said: "O God!" (?)
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: The hunt and games are abandoned as the king returns to his palace in deep gloom.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფე საწოლს შემოვიდა სევდიანი, დაღრეჯილი;
მისგან კიდე არვინ შეჰყვა, ავთანდილ უჩნს ვითა შვილი.
ყველაკაი გაიყარა, ჯალაბი ჩანს არ დაჯრილი.
და გაბედითდა სიხარული, ჩაღანა და ჩანგი ტკბილი.
stanzas.english_translation: The king went into his bedchamber sad and frowning. Avt’handil watched like a son that none save himself should follow; all went away, the household dispersed; merriment ceased, the castanet and the sweet harp.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan withdraws to his chamber attended only by Avtandil, while the court's music—the 'chaghana' (bowed/stringed instrument) and 'changi' (Georgian harp)—falls silent.

stanzas.english_translation: T’hinat’hin heard of her father's great sadness. She rose and came to the door; she with whom the sun strove asked the chamberlain: "Sleeps he or wakes he?" He answered: "He sits brooding; his colour has suffered a change.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Hearing of her father's grief, Tinatin comes to his chamber door and discreetly questions the chamberlain ('molare').

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ერთიღა ახლავს ავთანდილ, წინაშე უზის სკამითა;
უცხო ყმა ვინმე უნახავს, ასრე დაღრეჯით ამით-ა”.
თინათინ ბრძანა: “აწ წავალ, შესლვა არ ჩემგან ჟამით-ა,
და მიკითხოს, ჰკადრე, იყო-თქო აქა ერთისა წამითა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "Avt’handil alone is present; he sits in a chair before, him. They have seen a certain stranger knight; this is the cause of his melancholy." T’hinat’hin said: "I will now depart; it is not time for me to go in. When he asks for me, say: 'She was here but now.'"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Learning that Rostevan is brooding over the stranger knight with only Avtandil present, Tinatin tactfully withdraws until summoned by her father.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ხანი გამოხდა, იკითხა: “ნეტარ, რასა იქმს ქალიო,
ჩემი ლხინი და ჯავარი, ჩემი სოფლისა წყალიო?”
მოლარე ჰკადრებს: “მოვიდა აწეღა ფერ-ნამკრთალიო,
და დაღრეჯით გცნა და მიბრუნდა წინაშე მომავალიო”.
stanzas.english_translation: Time passed; he inquired: "What doth the maiden, my solace and jewel, my water of life?" The chamberlain replied: "She came, pale-faced, but now; she learned of your sadness and went away, but she is ready to come to your presence."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan asks after his daughter, calling her 'my joy, my jewel ('javari'), and my water of life.'

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
უბრძანა თუ: “წადი, უხმე, უმისობა ვით გავძლეო!
მოახსენე, რად დაბრუნდი, შენ, მამისა სიცოცხლეო?
მოდი, ჭმუნვა გამიქარვე, გულსა წყლულსა მეწამლეო,
და გითხრა ჩემი სამიზეზო, მე თუ ლხინთა რად დავლეო”.
stanzas.english_translation: He said: "Go, call her; how can I bear absence from her! Say unto her: 'Why didst thou turn back, O life of thy father? Come, drive away my grief, heal my wounded heart. I will tell thee wherefore my joy fled.'"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan summons Tinatin to comfort his wounded heart and hear the cause of his grief.

stanzas.english_translation: T’hinat’hin rose and came; she did as her father wished. The light of her face is like the splendour of the moon. Her father set her by his side, and, kissing her tenderly, gently, said: "Why tamest thou not to me? wert thou waiting till I sent for thee?"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan seats Tinatin beside him and affectionately asks why she waited for a summons.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ქალმან ჰკადრა: “ხელმწიფეო, დაღრეჯილსა ვინცა გცნობდეს,
ვინმცა გნახა კადნიერად, რაზომ გინდა ამაყობდეს!
თქვენნი აგრე დაღრეჯანი მნათობთაცა დაამხობდეს,
და კაცმან საქმე მოიგვაროს, ვეჭვ, ჭმუნვასა ესე სჯობდეს”.
stanzas.english_translation: The maiden said: "O king, who, however venturesome, would dare to approach you aware that you were frowning? This sadness of yours upsets even the lights of heaven. Let a man seek to solve the difficulty; this, I think, would be better than grieving."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Tinatin replies with both deference and active Renaissance rationality: rather than surrendering to passive grief ('chmunva'), a person should seek a practical remedy for the problem ('katsman sakme moigvaros, vechv, chmunvasa ese sjobdes').

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
უბრძანა: “შვილო, რაზომცა მჭირს საქმე სავაგლახია,
შენი ჭვრეტა და სიახლე ლხინადვე დამისახია,
მომაქარვები სევდისა, მართ ვითა მუფარახია,
და ვეჭვ, რა სცნა, შენცა მამართლო, ჩემი სულთქმა და ახია.
stanzas.english_translation: He answered: "O my child, however much this sad affair grieves me, thy sight and life cause me joy. My grief is dissipated as if I had taken an electuary. I believe that when thou knowest thou too wilt justify my sighing and groaning.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan compares Tinatin's comforting presence to 'muparakhi' (an Arabic-Persian medicinal cordial/electuary used to dispel melancholy) and begins recounting his encounter.

stanzas.english_translation: "I met a certain beautiful, wondrous youth; his ray enlightened the firmament and the bounds of the earth. I could not find out why he was afflicted, nor for whom he wept. He came not to see me; I was irritated and quarrelled with him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan describes the stranger knight's superhuman radiance and admits that he grew angry when the youth refused to come before him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე რა მნახა, ცხენსა შეჯდა, თვალთა ცრემლნი მოიხოცნა;
შესაპყრობლად შევუზახენ, სპანი სრულად დამიხოცნა,
ვითა ეშმა დამეკარგა, არ კაცურად გარდამკოცნა,
და ჯერთცა ესე არა ვიცი, ცხადი იყო, თუ მეოცნა.
stanzas.english_translation: "When he saw me, he mounted his horse and wiped the tears from his eyes. I cried out that he must be seized; he utterly destroyed my men; like an evil spirit, he was lost to me, he saluted me not like a man. Even now I know not whether he was real or a vision.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan recounts how the knight routed his troops and vanished like a spirit ('eshma'), leaving him uncertain whether the encounter was waking reality ('tskhadi') or an apparition ('meotsna').
Perplexed as to how a mortal of flesh could vanish without a trace after slaying his soldiers, Rostevan concludes that God has turned against him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ტკბილნი მისნი წყალობანი ბოლოდ ასრე გამემწარნეს,
დამავიწყდა, რაცა დღენი მხიარულსა წამეარნეს,
ყოვლმან პირმან ვაგლახ მიყოს, ვეღარავინ მინეტარნეს,
და სადამდისცა დღენი მესხნენ, ვეღარამან გამახარნეს!”
stanzas.english_translation: "His (God's) tender mercies at length have become thus bitter to me; I have forgotten the past days of my joy. Every one will make me sad and comfort me no more. However long my days may be, I can no more rejoice."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan despairs that this single humiliation has embittered all the former blessings of his reign.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ქალმან ჰკადრა: “მოგახსენებ მე სიტყვასა დანაყბედსა:
ჰე, მეფეო! რად ემდურვი ანუ ღმერთსა, ანუ ბედსა,
რად დასწამებ სიმწარესა ყოველთათვის ტკბილად მხედსა?
და ბოროტიმცა რად შეექმნა კეთილისა შემოქმედსა?
stanzas.english_translation: The maid replied: "Deign to hearken to my uttered words. O king, why repine at God or fate! Why accuse of bitterness the All-seeing, who is tender to all! And why should the Creator of good make evil:
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: As Academician Elguja Khintibidze highlights in the Georgian Encyclopedia, Line 4 ('Borotimtsa rad sheekmna ketilisa shemokmedsa?' — 'Why should the Creator of good have created evil?') formulates the foundational Christian-Neoplatonic theological doctrine (developed by St. Basil the Great, St. Gregory of Nyssa, Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, and Ioane Petritsi) that God is the Creator solely of the Good and that evil has no substantial divine creation or essence.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე ამას ვარჩევ: მეფე ხარ, მეფეთა ზედა მფლობელი,
შორს არის თქვენი საზღვარი, ბრძანება-მიუთხრობელი,
გაგზავნე კაცი ყოველგან მისთა ამბავთა მცნობელი,
და ადრე სცნობ, არის იგი ყმა შობილი, თუ უშობელი”.
stanzas.english_translation: "If this knight was indeed (a man) of flesh wandering over the earth, others must have seen him; they will appear to instruct you. If not, it is a devil who has appeared to you to disturb your joys. Refrain from sadness. Why art thou become cheerless?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Tinatin proposes an empirical investigation: dispatching envoys to all four corners of the earth to determine whether the stranger is a mortal born of woman ('shobili') or a bodiless apparition ('ushobeli').

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მოასხნეს კაცნი, გაგზავნეს ოთხთავე ცისა კიდეთა;
უბრძანეს: “წადით, პატიჟთა თავიმცა რად დაჰრიდეთა!
მონახეთ, ძებნეთ იგი ყმა, სხვად ნურად მოიცლიდეთა,
და მისწერეთ წიგნი, სადაცა ვერ მისწვდეთ, ვერ მიხვიდეთა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "This is my advice: Thou art king, ruler over kings; wide is your boundary, boundless is your power; send everywhere men with news of this story; soon shall you know whether this youth be a mortal or not."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Following Tinatin's counsel, Rostevan dispatches messengers across the world to search for the stranger.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
კაცნი წავიდეს, იარეს მათ ერთი წელიწადია,
მონახეს, ძებნეს იგი ყმა, იკითხეს კვლა და კვლა დია,
ვერ ნახეს მისი მნახავი ღმრთისაგან დანაბადია,
და ცუდად მაშვრალნი მოვიდეს, მათსავე გულსა ზადია.
stanzas.english_translation: He commanded men and sent them forth even to the four corners of the heavens, saying: "Go, spare yourselves no pains; search, hunt for that youth, let nothing hinder you; send a letter whither ye cannot go nor attain."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: For a full year the royal messengers search in vain without finding anyone who has seen the mysterious knight.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მონათა ჰკადრეს: “მეფეო, ჩვენ ხმელნი მოვიარენით,
მაგრა ვერ ვპოვეთ იგი ყმა, მით ვერა გავიხარენით,
მისსა მნახავსა სულ-დგმულსა კაცსა ვერ შევეყარენით,
და ჩვენ ვერა გარგეთ, საქმენი სხვანი რამ მოიგვარენით”.
stanzas.english_translation: The men went, they wandered about for a year; they looked, they sought that youth, they inquired again and again. They could find none of God's creatures who had seen him. Wearied in vain, they returned, dissatisfied with themselves.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: The envoys report their failure to the king.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფე ბრძანებს: “მართალ იყო ასული და ჩემი ძეო,
ვნახე რამე ეშმაკისა სიცრუვე და სიბილწეო,
ჩემად მტერად წამოსრული, გარდმოჭრილი ზეცით ზეო,
და გამიშვია შეჭირვება, არა მგამა ყოლა მეო”.
stanzas.english_translation: The slaves said: "O king, we have wandered over the lands, yet could we not find that youth, so we could not rejoice; we could meet no living man who had seen him; we have not been able to serve you, now devise some other plan."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Accepting the hypothesis that the apparition was a demonic illusion rather than a mortal knight, Rostevan casts off his sorrow.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ესე თქვა და სიხარულით თამაშობა ადიადა,
მგოსანი და მოშაითი უხმეს, პოვეს, რაცა სადა;
დია გასცა საბოძვარი, ყველა დარბაზს შემოხადა,
და მისი მსგავსი სიუხვითა ღმერთმან სხვამცა რა დაბადა!
stanzas.english_translation: The king replied: "My daughter, my child, spoke truth. I have seen a hideous, unclean spirit; he has been sent as my foe, flying down from heaven. Grief is fled from. me; I care nothing for all that."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Rostevan resumes his royal festivities, summoning minstrels ('mgosani') and acrobats ('moshaiti') and lavishing gifts upon the court, while Tinatin prepares in the next chapter to entrust the true quest to Avtandil.

act_title: Act I: Arabia, The Royal Hunt & Quest for the Stranger Knight

location.desc: Where Rostevan and Avtandil first behold the weeping Knight in the Panther's Skin.

key_maxim_ka: კაცმან საქმე მოიგვაროს, ვეჭვ, ჭმუნვასა ესე სჯობდეს
key_maxim_en: Let a man contrive a deed; I think this is better than grieving. (Stanza 114)
